name: Statutory authorization

subjectOf.text: Although shareholder agreements are authorized and shaped by corporation code provisions, their construction is governed by ordinary contract interpretation rules, so statutory authorization does not displace contract doctrine.
subjectOf.abstract: While the agreements are governed by legislation, general rules applicable to contract interpretation govern the construction of shareholder agreements.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Shareholder Agreements - National Report of the United States of America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3017612
scope_conditions: United States, Delaware law illustrated by Salamone v. Gorman

subjectOf.text: MBCA Section 7.32 requires unanimity, so agreements that bind only a block of shareholders rather than all of them cannot rely on that section and must find authorization elsewhere.
subjectOf.abstract: Most importantly the agreement must be unanimous, so that agreements that do not involve all shareholders, such as agreements designed to keep control within a block, must look elsewhere for their authorization.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Shareholder Agreements - National Report of the United States of America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3017612
